Ask What It Has Earned. We keep asking what AI agents can do. The harder question is what they have earned the right to do without us. Divya Sabade 9 min read · Just now -- Listen Share Photo by Kamil on Unsplash A few years ago I built systems that scored marketplace sellers for risk. The model would return a verdict: Seller Risk = HIGH. Underneath it, one line of explanation. The model detected anomalous behavior. A trust and safety analyst had a few minutes to decide what to do. Suspend the seller. Or override the flag and let them keep selling. Most of the time the model was right. That was never really the hard part. The hard part was a question nobody on my team had actually written down: Even if the model is right 99 times out of 100, should it be the one hitting suspend on the hundredth seller, on its own, with no analyst awake to catch it if it is wrong? We never gave the model that authority. We built it to recommend. We left a human to act. At the time I thought that was just caution. Here is the version everyone is living through right now.
